'''''Piper auritum''''' is an aromatic culinary [[herb]] in the pepper family [[Piperaceae]], which grows in and is endemic to tropical [[Central America]]. Common names include '''{{Lang|es|hoja santa}}''' ({{Langnf|es||sacred leaf}}),<ref name=Rolland/> '''{{Lang|es|yerba santa}}''',<ref name=miller>{{cite book | title = Coyote's Pantry: Southwest Seasonings and at Home Flavoring Techniques | first = Mark Charles | last = Miller | publisher = Ten Speed Press | year = 1993 | isbn = 0-89815-494-4 | page = [https://archive.org/details/coyotespantrysou0000mill/page/70 70] | url = https://archive.org/details/coyotespantrysou0000mill/page/70 }}</ref><ref name= katzer/> '''{{Lang|es|hierba santa}}''',<ref name=miller/> '''Mexican pepperleaf''',<ref name= katzer/> '''acuyo''',<ref name= katzer/> '''tlanepa''',<ref name= katzer/> '''anisillo''',<ref name= katzer/> '''root beer plant''',<ref name=Rolland/> '''Vera Cruz pepper,'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=PIAU|taxon=Piper auritum|access-date=6 October 2015}}</ref> '''sacred pepper,'''<ref name="barlow" /> and '''juniapa'''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ASALE |first=RAE- |last2=RAE |title=juniapa {{!}} Diccionario de la lengua española |url=https://dle.rae.es/juniapa |access-date=2026-06-08 |website=«Diccionario de la lengua española» - Edición del Tricentenario |language=es}}</ref>

== Description ==
It is a [[perennial]] herbaceous plant up to {{cvt|6|m}} in height with heart-shaped velvety leaves. The leaves can reach up to {{cvt|30|cm}} or more in size. The flowers are in simple white spikes containing myriads of tiny [[florets]] which rise above the foliage like candles.<ref>{{cite book |last=Zuchowski |first=Willow |title=Tropical Plants of Costa Rica |date=2007 |publisher=Cornell Univ. Press |isbn=978-0801445880 |location=Ithaca, N.Y. |pages=64-65}}</ref>

The entire plant is said to have the fragrance of [[Sassafras]]. === Chemistry ===
The leaf oil of ''Piper auritum'' contains a relatively high concentration of hepatotoxic [[safrole]], around 70%.  A few of the other 40 constituents occurring in minor quantities were [[α-thujene]], [[α-pinene]], [[camphene]], [[β-pinene]], [[myrcene]], and [[limonene]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gupta |first1=Mahabir P. |last2=Arias |first2=Tomás D. |last3=Williams |first3=Norris H. |last4=Bos |first4=R. |last5=Tattje |first5=D. H. E. |title=Safrole, the Main Component of the Essential Oil from Piper auritum of Panama |journal=Journal of Natural Products |date=March 1985 |volume=48 |issue=2 |pages=330–330 |doi=10.1021/np50038a026}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
It is native to the Americas, from northern South America to Mexico, and is also cultivated in California and southeast Florida.

== Uses ==
It is often used in [[Mexican cuisine]] in [[tamales]], fish or meat wrapped in its fragrant leaves for cooking, and as an essential ingredient in [[mole verde]], a green sauce originally from the [[Puebla/Oaxaca]] region of Mexico.<ref name="miller" /> It is also used to flavor eggs and soups like [[pozole]].<ref name="creasy">{{cite book |last=Creasy |first=Rosalind |title=The Edible Mexican Garden |publisher=Tuttle Publishing |year=2000 |isbn=962-593-297-6 |page=35}}</ref> In Central Mexico, it is used to flavor [[chocolate]] drinks.<ref name="katzer" /> In southeastern Mexico, a green [[liquor]] called '''verdín''' is made from hoja santa.<ref>{{cite web |last=Conner |first=Lori |year=2006 |title=El Restaurante Mexicano (May/June 2006): Beyond margaritas |url=http://www.restmex.com/recipes/0603.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070420024249/http://www.restmex.com/recipes/0603.shtml |archive-date=2007-04-20 |access-date=2007-04-01 |publisher=Maiden Name Press LLC}}</ref>

While typically used fresh, it is also used dried, although the drying process removes much of the flavor and makes the leaf too brittle to be used as a wrapper.<ref>{{cite book |last=Bladholm |first=Linda |url=https://archive.org/details/latincaribbeangr00lind/page/106 |title=Latin & Caribbean Grocery Stores Demystified |publisher=Renaissance Books |year=2001 |isbn=1-58063-212-2 |page=[https://archive.org/details/latincaribbeangr00lind/page/106 106]}}</ref>
